correctness.rationale: For squared sides s_i>0, Z=D²=Σ_i s_iW_i with W=(U-V)² and E(W^k)=2/((2k+1)(2k+2)). Direct integration gives κ1(W)=1/6, κ2(W)=7/180, κ3(W)=11/945; hence the displayed S1=6M2,S2=(180/7)(M4−M2²),S3=(945/11)(M6−3M4M2+2M2³) equal Σs_i^j. Newton yields the cubic with all roots positive, even at multiplicities. With r_i=s_i/S1, u=Σr_i²,v=Σr_i³, a real-rooted normalized cubic q(z)=z³−z²+(1−u)z/2−(1−3u+2v)/6 has discriminant nonnegative iff |v−(u−2/9)|≤[2(3u−1)]^{3/2}/36. Positive product v>(3u−1)/2 and positive pair sum with total 1 force all roots positive; for 1/3<u<1/2 the discriminant interval is entirely positive; at u=1/2 zero-edge lower equality is excluded; cube is u=1/3,v=1/9. Volume²=s1s2s3=36M2³(1−3u+2v). Distinct triples (1±2t,1∓t,1∓t) share M2,M4 but differ in M6 by 44t³/315. For δ in (0,1/2), R=(2δ)^{1/3} and Rouché on union of old-root radius-R disks proves equal root counts by components because |q|≥2δ>|q−qtilde| there; each component has length ≤6R and sorted real roots match. Larger δ bound trivial. Near the cube, the ±t triples have normalized sorted-root gap 2t/3 and δ=4t³/9, ruling out any exponent >1/3. All boundaries, quantifiers and degeneracy restrictions checked.

originality.rationale: A full 2007 primary forward density for varying box sides is important prior coverage and is explicitly credited. Its law gives ALL distance moments and the complete distance distribution; the new finite-observation claim is specifically that three even moments suffice, two do not, with the exact attainable normalized (u,v) domain and optimal global inverse exponent 1/3. Those assertions are not stated in the inspected Philip primary report. Abas 2026 proves three-cumulant inversion for spherical directional widths, not two-point interior distances. Classical cumulants, Newton inversion, cubic discriminant and general root continuity are not claimed as novel by themselves. No direct prior theorem covering the combined finite-statistic distance-moment statement was found in actual primary/source/corpus searches. Because full-law data is stronger, originality is restricted to minimal-data recovery and sharp feasible/stability specification, with a real risk that these are elementary corollaries of established forward formulas.
residual_risks: Johan Philip (2007) already provides a full forward distance law for ALL three-parameter rectangular boxes, with the same independent-coordinate convolution and an explicit second moment; the standalone three-moment cutoff is not explicitly stated there, but its moments can be derived from that stronger forward law using standard algebra. Priority is assigned only to the assembled minimal-data inverse, exact feasible region, and sharp uniform geometric modulus, not to the sampling distribution or cumulant machinery.

The 1/3 exponent follows generic cubic root coalescence; it is mathematically sharp here but the generic root-perturbation theorem is not new, and equivalent box-specific stability estimates might be unindexed.

value.rationale: Given an unlabeled one-dimensional point-pair distance statistic from a nondegenerate orthogonal box, the natural inverse task is to recover the three side lengths. Determining the exact minimal initial even-moment cutoff is a motivated finite-statistic identifiability question; two moments have a continuum of incompatible boxes, three recover the exact geometry. The complete physically realizable normalized-moment region identifies consistent data and the exact boundary where a dimension collapses; the sharp 1/3 Hölder exponent gives intrinsic ill-conditioning at cubes. These are coherent natural geometric-statistical invariants beyond quoting a cube table, even though elementary cumulants/Newton/root stability are the proof tools and the full forward density is long known. No general downstream paper-size result is required.
residual_risks: Generic cubic root stability is standard; mathematical value attaches to its sharp realization in this specific natural inverse observation, not an original root perturbation technique.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate 3D Euclidean orthogonal box with independent volume-uniform X,Y, the first three even distance moments (M2,M4,M6) determine the unordered strictly positive squared edge lengths as the roots of z³−S1z²+(S1²−S2)z/2−(S1³−3S1S2+2S3)/6, where S1=6M2, S2=(180/7)(M4−M2²), S3=(945/11)(M6−3M4M2+2M2³). Two even moments do not suffice. For u=(5/7)(M4/M2²−1),v=(35/88)(M6/M2³−3M4/M2²+2), exact feasibility is the given cusp u=1/3,v=1/9 or 1/3<u<1/2 with u−2/9−H(u)≤v≤u−2/9+H(u) or 1/2≤u<1 with (3u−1)/2<v≤u−2/9+H(u), H(u)=[2(3u−1)]^{3/2}/36. Volume²=36M2³(1−3u+2v). Normalized squared side lengths have globally uniform 1/3 Hölder inverse bound max|r_i−rtilde_i|≤6(2(|u−utilde|+|v−vtilde|))^{1/3}, optimal near cubes.
